key_insight: DeepFEAv2 extends deep-learning surrogate modeling for transient finite element analysis from structured meshes to both structured and unstructured FE topologies while jointly predicting node- and element-based outputs over time.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster transient simulation for complex mechanical systems, making near-real-time analysis more feasible without sacrificing high predictive accuracy.
method: Uses the finite element connectivity matrix to group inputs by element and sequence them according to mesh topology.
Employs a neural architecture tailored to process this topology-aware sequence and jointly predict NEO over time.
Adds a FEA-informed optimization strategy to regularize the predicted node- and element-level outputs.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on structured and unstructured 3D linear elastic datasets and a pressure-driven aortic valve dataset, achieving R^2 up to 0.99, normalized error as low as 0.38%, and inference up to three orders of magnitude faster than traditional FEA.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and consistency of mesh connectivity encoding, so generalization to highly irregular meshes or unseen element types may require careful validation.
paper_title: DeepFEAv2: Deep Learning for Transient Finite Element Analysis Beyond Structured Meshes
